Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is normally **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
- When both regions observe daylight‑saving time (PDT = UTC‑7, CEST = UTC+2) the gap stays 9 hours.  
- During the brief overlap periods when one region has switched to DST and the other has not (e.g., early March or late October/early November), the difference can temporarily be 8 hours.  

So, for most of the year you can think of Los Angeles as 9 hours behind Berlin.
